oil.summary: Brent crossed the $100/bbl threshold for the first time in nearly two months in Asian trade Wednesday, closing at $100.56 (+2.70%) while WTI settled at $95.67 (+2.84%), extending a month-long rally of roughly 15-16%. The primary driver remains Middle East escalation: Iran has threatened the US with 'economic warfare' and missiles, Houthis have attacked Saudi Arabia, and collapsing hopes for US-Iran talks are sustaining a meaningful geopolitical risk premium. Heating oil surged 4.22% to $4.76/gal on tightening diesel fundamentals, with industry warnings of a worsening refining capacity shortfall. RBOB gasoline was the notable outlier, plunging 6.67%, suggesting demand-side pressure at the pump. Sinopec's projection of an 8.9% drop in Chinese oil demand for 2026 and Iraq's push for a larger OPEC quota add medium-term complexity. Morgan Stanley notes traders are avoiding longer-dated exposure given unresolved war uncertainty.
drivers: Middle East escalation — Iran-US tensions and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia — driving a sustained geopolitical risk premium pushing Brent through $100/bbl
Diesel crunch deepening: India running refineries at 105-108% capacity, global refining shortfall warnings, and heating oil hitting $4.76/gal (+4.22%)
Demand headwinds emerging: Sinopec forecasts China oil demand -8.9% in 2026, and RBOB gasoline fell sharply 6.67% on the day

gas.summary: The gas picture today presents a sharp transatlantic divergence. TTF surged 4.12% on the day to €78.97/MWh, extending a blistering +29.88% monthly gain, almost certainly reflecting spillover from Middle East supply anxiety and broader European energy security concerns tied to the ongoing conflict environment. Henry Hub, by contrast, slid 2.57% to $2.842/MMBtu, remaining under modest pressure with only a marginal 1.68% monthly gain — suggesting US domestic fundamentals remain loose. Headline flow for the gas sector is thin today; the most relevant item is the expected arrival of Qatari LNG in Pakistan this month following navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, signaling that LNG flows are continuing despite regional tensions. ExxonMobil's 20th discovery in Angola's Block 15 is a longer-dated supply story with no near-term pricing impact.
drivers: TTF extending a sharp monthly rally (+29.88%) driven by European supply security concerns linked to Middle East escalation and Russia-Ukraine conflict
Henry Hub softening (-2.57% on the day) as US domestic fundamentals remain comparatively loose, diverging strongly from European benchmarks
Qatari LNG successfully transiting Hormuz toward Pakistan, indicating key LNG trade lanes remain open despite regional hostilities

power.summary: EU Carbon EUAs edged up 0.95% to $80.59/EUA, supported by the continued surge in TTF gas prices (+4.12% today, +29.88% on the month), which raises the cost of gas-fired generation and mechanically lifts carbon abatement incentives. On the demand side, a California heat wave is testing the grid as the National Weather Service issues broad heat advisories across the Central Valley, Bay Area, and Los Angeles. The most significant structural story is Google's commitment to invest at least €13 billion in Finnish AI infrastructure over 2027-2028, anchored by a 22-year power purchase agreement tied to Finnish nuclear capacity — a major long-dated signal of data-center-driven nuclear power demand. UK sanctions on Russia's Transneft add modest additional uncertainty to Russian energy flows, though direct power market impact today is limited.
drivers: TTF gas spike (+4.12% to €78.97/MWh) lifting power generation costs across Europe and supporting EUA carbon prices
California heat wave driving demand surge and grid stress, adding near-term upward pressure on US power markets
Google's €13bn Finnish AI infrastructure investment with a 22-year nuclear PPA signals accelerating long-term data-center demand for clean firm power
